page.description: SliTaz editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A minimalist, ultra-lightweight Linux distribution that runs entirely in RAM. Desktop under 70 MB, boots in seconds, and includes a package manager with thousands of packages.
pros: Extremely lightweight – full desktop under 70 MB
Boots in seconds and runs entirely in RAM
Thousands of packages available via spk package manager
Multiple flavors: core, firefox, base, and retro
cons: Checksums only provided as MD5, no SHA-256 available
Very small download mirrors with limited bandwidth
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for SliTaz; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the ISO to a USB stick with dd or Rufus. Boot from BIOS or UEFI. The entire system loads into RAM, leaving the USB free for data storage.

editions.name: Core (x86_64)
editions.description: Minimal 64-bit edition with LXTaz desktop – the fastest SliTaz experience.
editions.usbNote: 66 MB image. Write it with dd or Rufus; writing erases the stick.

editions.name: Firefox (x86_64)
editions.description: Core edition plus Firefox ESR and additional applications for daily use.
editions.usbNote: 153 MB image. Write it with dd or Rufus; writing erases the stick.

editions.name: Core (i486)
editions.description: 32-bit edition for older PCs – same minimal LXTaz desktop on 32-bit hardware.

editions.name: Base
editions.description: Text-mode system without a graphical server, for servers, rescue work or very old machines.
